blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: firewall — Security control that permits or blocks network traffic according to rules.
forward proxy — Intermediary that makes requests on a client's behalf.
filter rule — A condition and action defining whether traffic is permitted.
cache — Stored copy of suitable data for reuse.
defence in depth — Use multiple complementary security controls rather than trusting one.

blocks.title: Check a firewall rule
blocks.text: A firewall applies configured rules to traffic according to properties such as direction, source/destination, ports and state. A basic rule example can allow TCP port 443 but deny 22.

blocks.title: Different request, different decision
blocks.text: A TCP connection to port 22 is denied by the illustrated policy. A firewall rule is not automatically a guarantee that the permitted service is safe.

blocks.title: A proxy is an intermediary
blocks.text: A forward proxy makes requests on behalf of clients, potentially enforcing policy or caching suitable resources. HTTPS content remains encrypted unless a controlled interception mechanism is in place.

blocks.title: Worked example · 443
blocks.text: An inbound TCP connection destined for port 443 matches the allow rule and is permitted.

blocks.title: Worked example · 22
blocks.text: An inbound TCP connection destined for port 22 matches the deny rule and is blocked.

blocks.title: Allowed resource
blocks.text: The student's request reaches the proxy, which permits it and contacts the website; a suitable cached response may be used instead.

blocks.title: Blocked resource
blocks.text: If the proxy's policy denies the destination, it does not forward the request to that site; the student receives a blocking response.
